q: What's the difference between net ROAS and the ROAS Meta shows, and which should I trust for budget decisions?
answer:
Net ROAS and Meta’s (platform-reported) ROAS are different measures with different uses: net ROAS (our net ROAS) is contribution before ads ÷ ad spend — a profit-side efficiency on the company books — while Meta’s ROAS is a placement/attribution view (gross-style) that credits gross sales to ads and is useful as an ad-delivery signal, not a company profit measure.

What that means
- Basis and timing: Net ROAS is available on a switchable date axis but is normally used on order date and is built from contribution_before_ads and ad spend (profit before ads ÷ spend). Gross/placement ROAS (the platform-style ROAS our catalogue calls gross ROAS) is placement-only attribution and credits gross sales at the placement time. Use net ROAS when you need the business P&L picture; gross ROAS when you want ad platform delivery signals (which campaign is driving attributed conversions right now).
- What each includes: Net ROAS accounts for product & fulfilment costs and other contribution lines (so it reflects the margin available to pay for ads). Meta’s ROAS (placement/gross) uses attributed gross sales and does not deduct COGS, fulfilment, returns or company-level deductions.
- Trust for budgets: rely on net ROAS for budget decisions tied to profitability (can we afford to scale this spend?). Use Meta’s ROAS as a high-frequency operational signal (which creatives/campaigns are converting in-platform) but reconcile it to net ROAS before increasing spend materially.
Worth checking: compare net ROAS and gross ROAS by ad_platform and campaign for the last 30 days to see which campaigns have big gaps (large gross ROAS but low or negative net ROAS).
